context.title: Extremal size and uniqueness conjecture for strongly-connected k-geodetic digraphs
context.statement:
Let $ex^*(n;k)$ denote the largest number of arcs in a strongly-connected $k$-geodetic digraph of order $n$, and let $G(kr,k)$ be the construction described in the paper. The **extremal size and uniqueness conjecture** asserts that, whenever

$$
n \geq k+1\quad\text{and}\quad n \leq (k+1)\left\lfloor \frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor,
$$

(in particular, for $n \geq k^2-k$),

$$
ex^*(n;k)=\left\lfloor \frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor^2-(k+2)\left\lfloor \frac{n}{k}\right\rfloor+2n.
$$

Moreover, for $r\geq 2$, the underlying graph of $G(kr,k)$ is the unique graph of largest size admitting a strongly-connected $k$-geodetic orientation. This conjecture proposes an exact extremal formula and a uniqueness statement for the constructions in the strongly-connected setting; the paper supplies bounds and computational evidence, but the claimed general extremality is not established.

context.title: Meyer equitable chromatic number conjecture
context.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. A proper equitable $t$-coloring is a proper vertex coloring whose color classes differ in size by at most one, and $\chi^{=}(G)$ is the least $t$ for which $G$ has a proper equitable $t$-coloring. **Meyer's conjecture.** If $G$ is neither a complete graph nor an odd cycle, then

$$
\chi^{=}(G)\leq \Delta(G).
$$

This is presented as a well-known conjecture on equitable colorings, attributed in the source to Meyer. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied material.
context.source_name: Jian-Liang Wu, Xin Zhang and Hailun Li, “Equitable vertex arboricity of graphs”, arXiv:1211.4193 (2012).
context.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1210.6568](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.6568).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4193

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2012).

context.title: Non-polynomial growth for k-dominating independent sets in incidence graphs of projective planes
context.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the family of incidence graphs of projective planes, and let $\text{mi}_k(n,\mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of $k$-dominating independent sets among $n$-vertex graphs in this family.

**Projective-plane incidence-graph conjecture.** The function $\text{mi}_k(n,\mathcal{F})$ is not bounded above by any polynomial in $n$.

This addresses the growth-rate alternatives posed for structured graph families and predicts superpolynomially many $k$-dominating independent sets in incidence graphs of projective planes. The source gives no resolution.
context.mathematics: Superpolynomial lower bound requires an infinite sequence of actual projective planes and k-dominating independent sets. No uniform independent family construction; fixed-plane counting cannot resolve growth.

context.title: Polynomial bound for spherical codes with a negative interval and k positive inner products
context.literal_statement:
Let $N_L(d)$ denote the maximum size of a spherical code in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose pairwise inner products belong to $L$. For $\beta$ and $k$ as in the conjecture, and for any real numbers $\alpha_1,\dotsc,\alpha_k$, set

$$
L=[-1,-\beta]\cup\{\alpha_1,\dotsc,\alpha_k\}.
$$

**Polynomial spherical-code conjecture.** Suppose $\alpha_1,\dotsc,\alpha_k$ are any $k$ real numbers. Then

$$
N_L(d)\leq c_{\beta,k}d^k.
$$

This extends the linear bound for a single allowed inner product and the constant bound for inner products in $[-1,-\beta]$. The conjectured degree-$k$ estimate is left open in the source.
context.mathematics: Need uniform polynomial d^k bound over all positive inner-product values with fixed beta>0,k. Source-domain parameters cannot be dropped to beta=0 or alpha=1 for a wording refutation. No rank/inertia polynomial resolving full endpoint.

context.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph. Write $\text{mi}_2(n)$ for the maximum number of $2$-dominating independent sets in an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\text{mi}_2(G)$ denote the number in $G$. Define $\zeta_2(n)$ as the corresponding exponential growth rate, and let $K_3\square K_3$ be the Cartesian product of two complete graphs.

**The $\sqrt[9]{6}$-conjecture.** The maximal number of $2$-dominating independent sets in $n$-vertex graphs is $\Theta(\sqrt[9]{6}^{\,n})$; equivalently,

$$
\zeta_2(n)=\zeta_2(K_3\square K_3).
$$

Moreover, Construction 1, consisting of disjoint unions of copies of $K_3\square K_3$ and $K_4\square K_4$, provides the extremal graphs for $\text{mi}_2(n)$ when $n$ is sufficiently large.

The conjecture identifies the asymptotically extremal product graphs and specifies the extremal constructions, strengthening the preceding lower bound. Its resolution would determine the precise exponential growth rate and the extremal graphs for the case $k=2$.
